title: Quantum Sphaera Companion: A Structure-First Mathematical Unfolding — full Companion and physics paper
description:
Quantum Sphaera Companion v5.4.0 is a minor version of the database-backed v5 release. As before, it comprises two complementary English documents from one source snapshot: the full Companion with its research history, and the physics paper Graded carriers and physical readouts: conditions for mass and geometric interpretation.

New in the full Companion are the research layers v4.10.0-r31 to r59. They record: the orientation of the octant step read as a time orientation, and why the Holst term and the frame maps do not fix the second counting rule (r31, r52); a worked case of the open problem OP5, in which an elastic preparation makes the ordinary linear gravitational response compact while a directed comparison channel still sees a contrast, under an assumed and not derived identification of the two sources (r32 to r35); a series of candidate mediators for the directed channel (vacuum background, stretched string, a first field-equation ansatz, a tensor-field reading) together with an audit of this chain and the choice behind it (r36 to r45); frame, axis and time orientation as readout data and their consequences for the matter frame and the comparison model (r46 to r51, r54); counting rules as a dimension formula, which requires the two extreme states of a puncture to act as distinct maps (r53); a map of how the open problems hang together (r55); a negative result for one remainder: within a named class of constructions of the record the value of the cosmological constant is an input (r56); a pre-registered, not blind comparison of a feedback cascade with DESI DR2 BAO data, which the data do not exclude but which fits worse than LambdaCDM (r57); a temporally ordered octant readout that does not supply the weight of the matter rule (r58); and a collected round of explorations on handedness and a Cayley-Dickson tower of Hilbert shifts, including a pre-registered prediction for the sign of the leptonic CP phase that rests on a setting and can be tested by about 2035 (r59).

New in the physics paper: a development section with the worked OP5 case in the geometry part; additions to the limits section on the Holst term and the frame map, the dimension reading of the counting rules, the readout gaps across the open problems, the cosmological constant as an input and the cascade comparison; and a short account of the handedness series in the masses part.

Scope: this is a conditional mathematical-physics research programme, not a completed unified theory. No native lepton spectrum, absolute physical mass scale, general gravitational field equations or closure of the open problems is established by this release. Most results of r31 to r59 are explorations, not blind tests; the tests that were pre-registered are marked as not blind where their outcome was foreseeable. The Koide overlap, the core size, the orientation of the octant step, the counting rule per frame and the identification of sources in the OP5 case remain open. Database registration, hashes and provenance checks do not constitute proof of physical interpretation. The manuscript has undergone documented self-review, not independent peer review.

The package contains two English PDFs, compilable sources, a database snapshot and checksum manifests. Both document editions retain open argument-review obligations.

Version DOI: to be assigned on reservation. Concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19210728.
notes: Two complementary English documents in one versioned Companion record. The version DOI identifies the whole package. The German reader edition is excluded. Scientific guards and incomplete argument-review flags remain unchanged. Reservation and upload do not constitute publication.
